data.narrative:
World Labs, a Series A artificial intelligence and software company founded by Fei-Fei Li, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner, and Justin Johnson, has raised $1.23B+ to date. The valuation analysis triangulates against a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR), with primary focus on same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies including Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, and Black Forest Labs.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base ($1.2B) and applying a typical Series A step-up multiplier of 2.0x, implies a valuation of $2.5B. Peer-median analysis across the four primary comparables yielded a median valuation of $15.3B, with a range spanning $3.2B (Black Forest Labs, Series B) to $29.0B (Scale AI, Series B). The wide peer dispersion reflects material stage and maturity variation within the frontier-AI cohort.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $2.1B (low) to $17.6B (high), with a median of $8.9B. Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage-adjustment discount relative to Series B peers commanding substantially higher valuations, and the degree to which World Labs' specific technology and market positioning should be reflected above or below peer medians. The 8.4x range between low and high reflects inherent volatility in frontier-tech pricing absent established financial performance or revenue benchmarks.
